text:
anya: Heads up — noticed routing-policy changes show up as a single blob in the audit export. We can't tell which rule evaluated or why quota fell back. Can we add row-level lineage and the policy decision_reason to the export?

kai: +1. Need the decision_reason (e.g. "route_by_latency", "tenant_priority") and the specific rule id. Right now console only shows a UI diff but exports give no runnable context.

maria: Are we talking about the NDJSON export or the downloadable bundle? I worry about payload size if we include full rule bodies for every change.

sam: Prefer NDJSON with a manifest file pointing to policy snapshots. Manifest can include policy_version, policy_hash, and a small decision_reason field per event. That keeps rows skinny but linkable.

olga: +1 to manifest approach. For compliance we also need the effective_config at time-of-change for replay. Maybe store policy snapshots in the export bundle under /policies/<hash>.json and reference by hash in the event lines.

anya: Example I had in mind: Each event row contains tenant_id, resource_id, change_ts, actor, change_set_id. Add fields: policy_hash, decision_reason, matched_rule_id. Then bundle includes policies/<policy_hash>.json.

sam: Exactly. Something like:

```
{ "tenant": "acme", "ts": "2026-03-17T14:02:33Z", "actor": "policy-engine@redwood", "event_type": "route_decision", "policy_hash": "sha256:abc123", "matched_rule": "route-42", "decision_reason": "quota_exhausted_burst_fallback" }
```

kai: That helps traceability. Also add a small `decision_metadata` map for transient metrics (e.g., `queue_depth`: 42, `latency_ms`: 120) so ops can triage without rehydrating whole snapshot. Keep it optional to avoid bloat.

maria: How do we handle PII in `actor` or `decision_metadata`? Some orgs log service accounts with emails. Need redaction modes or pseudonymization toggles in export settings.

olga: We already surfaced a `pii_mode` in console for downloads. Exports can accept `pii_mode: [redact,pseudonymize,plain]`. For pseudonymize we emit `actor_pseudonym` and a separate key in the bundle `pseudonym_map.json` available to tenant admins.

anya: Nice. A few operational concerns: export generation time (can blow up if we snapshot many policy versions). We should only include snapshots actually referenced by events in the export time window. Also cap manifest size and provide pagination.

sam: On pagination: NDJSON streams are easiest for consumers, but for large date ranges we should support chunked bundles with a top-level `export_manifest.json` listing parts and checksums. Then consumers can download specific parts.

kai: Audit retention interplay — if a referenced policy snapshot expired from our long-term store we either need to embed the snapshot in the export or mark as `snapshot_unavailable`. Compliance teams will want embedding by default. Maybe an enterprise toggle: `embed_snapshots: true|false`.

maria: UX question for console: show a compact `who/what/why` summary per event and an expand to view the referenced policy (rendered). Also allow direct link to pre-signed policy JSON in bundle.

olga: Security: pre-signed links TTL must match export retention policy. Also sign the bundle manifest with a key so customers can verify integrity (enterprise requirement).

anya: Telemetry needs: we should emit a telemetry event whenever a download or stream includes policy snapshots (counts, total_bytes, number_of_snapshots) for billing/ops. Add `export.metrics.snapshots_included` and `export.metrics.bytes` to our existing metrics.

sam: For API shape, I'd propose adding query params to our export endpoint: `?embed_snapshots=true&pii_mode=pseudonymize&chunk_size=10000`. And in payload we return `manifest` + `parts` array (if chunked). Keep backward compatibility by defaulting to current compact export shape.

kai: Internal API debate: should `decision_reason` live at top-level event or inside a `routing_decision` field? Top-level is easier for ad-hoc parsing but less structured. I vote `routing_decision` object `{ reason, matched_rule, metadata }` to allow future fields without breaking.

maria: I second structured object. Consumers can still pick flat keys if they want. Document clearly in API docs.

olga: Implementation notes: exporter service will need to resolve policy references by hash at export time. Add a jittered background fetch if snapshot missing. Also ensure access checks — only include snapshots if tenant owns them (don't leak cross-tenant snapshots).

anya: Can we add a small sample in docs repo for compliance teams? Sam, Kai — could you sketch the NDJSON sample + manifest? Then I can wire it into console mockups.

sam: I'll sketch it today. Quick sample manifest idea:

```
{
  "export_id": "exp-2469-001",
  "time_range": ["2026-03-01", "2026-03-17"],
  "parts": ["part-000.ndjson", "part-001.ndjson"],
  "policies": { "sha256:abc123": "policies/sha256_abc123.json" }
}
```

kai: I'll add the structured `routing_decision` object to the API spec PR. Will also add a flag to redact sensitive keys in `decision_metadata` by default.

deploy-bot: deploy 2469123570 started by @kai — export-api v2 (manifest + snapshot refs)

olga: After deploy we should run an internal export against staging tenant to validate bundle size and manifest integrity. I'll schedule it.

anya: Thanks all. Main action items: sam + kai sample files; olga schedule validation; maria update console mock; anya will draft proto spec for export query params and PII modes.

maria: ping me when draft is ready, I'll wire UI affordances (toggle embed snapshots, pii mode dropdown). :thumbsup:

sam: putting sample NDJSON and manifest in docs repo branch `audit-export-policy-snapshots` later today.

anya: Great — we'll regroup after staging run.
